meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.name: Prostate cancer
data.description: Cancer in which oncogenic mTOR signaling reprograms the cell's translation to drive proliferation, invasion and metastasis.
data.description_beginner: A cancer in which mTOR signaling gets hijacked to rev up a tumor's protein-building machinery, helping it grow, invade nearby tissue, and spread.

studies.title: The translational landscape of mTOR signalling steers cancer initiation and metastasis
studies.authors: Hsieh AC; Liu Yi; Edlind MP; Ingolia NT; Janes MR; Sher A; et al.; Ruggero D

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Showed WHY mTOR-driven translation matters for cancer: in prostate cancer, oncogenic mTOR selectively translates a specific set of pro-invasion mRNAs that drive metastasis. An ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor (INK128) reversed that signature - an early preclinical rationale from mouse models and cell lines, not a clinical result.

relations.mechanism: Blocking mTOR reversed Akt-driven pre-cancerous prostate lesions in mice, showing the growth was mTORC1-dependent and reversible.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Blocking mTOR reversed early, pre-cancerous prostate changes in mice caused by an overactive growth signal.
relations.boundary: Scope: the lesion was prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia, a pre-cancerous stage, driven by transgenic human AKT1 in mice, and the drug (RAD001) inhibits mTORC1 allosterically. Not a demonstration in established prostate cancer.

relations.mechanism: Prostate tumours driven by Pten loss need mTORC2 specifically - normal prostate does not. A real therapeutic window, at least in mice.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Prostate tumours caused by losing a specific tumour-suppressor gene specifically need mTORC2 to grow – normal prostate tissue doesn't, at least in mice.
